:::{#def-idempotent-matrix}
#### Idempotent matrix

A square matrix $\matr{A}$ is **idempotent** if

$$\matr{A}^2 = \matr{A}$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-idempotent}
#### An idempotent matrix

For $\matr{P} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$,

$$
\ba
\matr{P}^2
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 \cd 1 + 0 \cd 0 & 1 \cd 0 + 0 \cd 0 \\ 0 \cd 1 + 0 \cd 0 & 0 \cd 0 + 0 \cd 0 \end{bmatrix}
&& \text{(definition of matrix multiplication)}
\\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \matr{P},
&& \text{(multiply and add)}
\ea
$$

so $\matr{P}$ is idempotent.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-not-idempotent}
#### A matrix that is not idempotent

For $\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\matr{A}^2
&= \begin{bmatrix} 2 \cd 2 + 0 \cd 0 & 2 \cd 0 + 0 \cd 0 \\ 0 \cd 2 + 0 \cd 0 & 0 \cd 0 + 0 \cd 0 \end{bmatrix} \\
&= \begin{bmatrix} 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\
&\ne \matr{A},
\end{aligned}
$$

so $\matr{A}$ is not idempotent.

:::
